title: Goblin Slayer Side Story: Year One
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A prequel to Goblin Slayer: a boy survives a goblin raid that destroys his village and kills his sister, is trained by a mysterious master, and five years later becomes a lowest-rank adventurer who takes only goblin-extermination quests. He reunites with his childhood friend Cow Girl as his single-minded war on goblins begins (Yen Press blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates; ANN).
life_message: Relentless purpose can protect others, though obsession born of trauma leaves little room for anything else.

content.note: Graphic village massacre and blow-by-blow battles (ANN); MU Blood and Gore, Torture, Genocide; AniList Gore 79.
'Bleak, brutal' string of traumatic events (ANN); MU Dark Fantasy, Horror genre.
Sexual violence against women depicted more explicitly than in the novel; gratuitous nudity of 13-year-old Cow Girl (ANN); MU Rape, Gang Rape, Nudity, Borderline H.
Grief and obsession after his family's death (Yen Press blurb; ANN; MU Obsession, Death of Loved One).

dominant: Revenge and obsession; trauma; protecting the weak from monsters

frames.aligns: He defends villages others ignore; the story shows goblin atrocities as evil.
frames.concerns: Explicit sexual violence and child nudity (ANN); revenge as life's purpose.
Graphic rape and gore; passions of vengeance.
Explicit sexual violence and nudity throughout.

frames.aligns: Helping those no one else will.
Victims taken seriously as a motive.
frames.concerns: Sexual violence used as spectacle; minor's nudity.

frames.aligns: Purifying a threat to the community.

frames.concerns: Anger as driving force; sexual content.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Personal vow of vengeance drives him (ANN; MU Revenge).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Works within guild ranks but alone (Yen Press blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Sister and village loss; bond with Cow Girl (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Starts at lowest adventurer rank (Yen Press blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Gods and magic exist; he relies on tactics.

folkways.japan: Based on a Japanese light novel in a tabletop-RPG style fantasy setting; the silent, single-purpose warrior echoes the lone avenger figure in Japanese fiction.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers say it fails to develop themes beyond its violence; obsession is shown, not argued.
delivery.note: Goblins are presented as pure monsters rather than a viewpoint, and the hero's obsession is shown without commentary.

winners_losers: The Slayer begins to succeed against goblins; villagers and women suffer heavily. Sympathy goes to the victims and their avenger.
